meta.description: MedLink curated OTC formulary for India. Only genuinely non-prescription (general-sale / Schedule OTC) medicines belong here. The LLM never picks from this list directly - src/medicine/filter.py applies hard safety filters and an allow-list gate, and the recommendation text is built only from these structured fields.
meta.review_note: Dosing figures are standard adult/paediatric OTC references. Must be verified against current CDSCO / national STG and a pharmacist before production use.

medicines.adult_dose: 1 tablet (500 mg) every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Do not take more than 4 grams (8 tablets) in 24 hours.
medicines.max_daily_dose: 4000 mg/day (adult); lower if low body weight, elderly, or regular alcohol use.
medicines.paediatric_dose: Use the paracetamol syrup for children instead of tablets. 15 mg per kg body weight per dose, up to 4 times a day.
interactions: warfarin (frequent high doses may raise bleeding risk)
other medicines that also contain paracetamol - do not combine
medicines.overdose_note: Even a modest overdose can cause fatal liver failure with few early symptoms. Seek hospital care immediately if too much has been taken.
medicines.source: WHO Model Formulary; Indian NLEM

medicines.strength: 250 mg / 5 mL (125 mg/5 mL also common)
medicines.adult_dose: Adults should use paracetamol tablets instead.
medicines.max_daily_dose: 60 mg per kg per day, not exceeding 4 doses in 24 hours.
medicines.paediatric_dose: 15 mg per kg per dose every 6 hours. Use the dosing cup/syringe in the pack and dose by weight, not age. For a 10 kg child that is about 3 mL of 250 mg/5 mL syrup.
contraindications: age under 2 months without a doctor
medicines.overdose_note: Measure with the syringe, never a kitchen spoon. Overdose causes liver damage - go to hospital if too much was given.
medicines.source: WHO IMCI; Indian Academy of Pediatrics

medicines.adult_dose: 1 tablet (400 mg) every 6 to 8 hours with or after food. Maximum 1200 mg/day without medical advice.
medicines.max_daily_dose: 1200 mg/day (OTC limit).
medicines.paediatric_dose: Not from this entry. Paediatric ibuprofen needs weight-based dosing and a doctor for young children.
contraindications: stomach ulcer or history of GI bleeding
aspirin or NSAID-triggered asthma or wheeze
interactions: ACE inhibitors / ARBs and diuretics (kidney risk)
major_side_effects: GI bleeding (black stools, vomiting blood - stop and seek care)
medicines.overdose_note: Large overdoses cause stomach bleeding, seizures and kidney injury - seek care.
medicines.source: WHO Model Formulary; NICE CKS NSAIDs

medicines.strength: 1 sachet per 1 litre of clean water

active_ingredients.name: sodium chloride + potassium chloride + trisodium citrate + glucose

medicines.adult_dose: Dissolve one sachet in exactly 1 litre of clean (boiled and cooled) water. Sip 200 to 400 mL after each loose stool. Discard any solution left after 24 hours.
medicines.max_daily_dose: As much as needed to replace losses and keep passing urine; there is no fixed limit.
medicines.paediatric_dose: After each loose stool: under 2 years about 50 to 100 mL, 2 to 10 years about 100 to 200 mL, older children as for adults. Continue breastfeeding and normal feeds.
contraindications: cannot drink at all or persistent vomiting (needs a clinic)
signs of severe dehydration (needs a clinic/hospital)
known kidney failure - use under medical advice
major_side_effects: mild vomiting if taken too fast - slow down and continue
medicines.overdose_note: Only dangerous if made too concentrated - always use a full litre of water per sachet.
medicines.source: WHO/UNICEF ORS guidance; IAP diarrhoea guidelines

medicines.adult_dose: Zinc for diarrhoea is a paediatric measure; adults should focus on ORS.
medicines.max_daily_dose: 20 mg/day for children over 6 months.
medicines.paediatric_dose: 2 to 6 months: 10 mg once daily for 14 days. Over 6 months: 20 mg once daily for 14 days. Dissolve in a little breast milk, ORS or clean water. Give WITH ORS, not instead of it.
interactions: reduces absorption of some antibiotics if taken together - separate by 2 hours
medicines.overdose_note: Very high single doses cause vomiting and stomach upset.
medicines.source: WHO/UNICEF; IAP

indications: short-term relief of frequent watery stools in adults with no fever and no blood in stool
medicines.adult_dose: 2 tablets (4 mg) first, then 1 tablet (2 mg) after each loose stool. Maximum 8 mg/day for self-care. ORS is still the main treatment.
medicines.max_daily_dose: 8 mg/day for self-care (up to 16 mg/day only under medical supervision).
medicines.paediatric_dose: Do not use for children from this entry.
contraindications: blood or mucus in the stool (dysentery)
suspected food poisoning with high fever
interactions: medicines that slow the heart or prolong QT (high-dose loperamide is cardiotoxic)
certain antifungals and antibiotics that raise loperamide levels
major_side_effects: dangerous heart rhythms if the dose is exceeded
medicines.overdose_note: Overdose can cause life-threatening heart rhythm problems. Never exceed the stated dose.
medicines.source: WHO Model Formulary; FDA loperamide safety communication

indications: itchy or watery eyes from allergy
itching from mild allergic skin rash
medicines.adult_dose: 1 tablet (10 mg) once daily, preferably at night as it can cause mild drowsiness.
medicines.max_daily_dose: 10 mg/day (adult).
medicines.paediatric_dose: 6 to 12 years: 5 mg once daily (or 5 mg twice daily). Use the syrup for younger children and only on a doctor's advice under 2 years.
interactions: alcohol and other sedating medicines increase drowsiness
medicines.overdose_note: Overdose causes marked drowsiness, restlessness in children, and fast heartbeat.
medicines.source: WHO Model Formulary; NICE CKS allergic rhinitis

medicines.adult_dose: 1 tablet (10 mg) once daily. Less sedating than cetirizine.
medicines.max_daily_dose: 10 mg/day (adult).
medicines.paediatric_dose: 2 to 12 years and over 30 kg: 10 mg once daily; under 30 kg: 5 mg once daily (syrup).
interactions: generally few; caution with strong CYP3A4/2D6 inhibitors
medicines.overdose_note: Overdose can cause fast heartbeat, drowsiness and headache.
medicines.source: WHO Model Formulary

medicines.generic_name: Antacid suspension (magnesium + aluminium hydroxide with simethicone)
medicines.adult_dose: 10 mL after meals and at bedtime when symptoms occur. Shake well before use.
medicines.max_daily_dose: Up to 4 times a day for short-term use.
medicines.paediatric_dose: Not from this entry for young children; use only on a doctor's advice under 12.
contraindications: severe kidney disease (magnesium and aluminium accumulate)
interactions: reduces absorption of many medicines - separate iron, thyroid tablets, many antibiotics (tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones) and some HIV/TB drugs by at least 2 hours
medicines.overdose_note: Chronic heavy use can disturb body salts, especially with poor kidney function.
medicines.source: WHO Model Formulary; NICE CKS dyspepsia

medicines.adult_dose: 1 to 2 tablets chewed when heartburn occurs.
medicines.max_daily_dose: Do not exceed the pack limit (usually about 7 tablets/day) or use for more than 2 weeks without advice.
medicines.paediatric_dose: Not from this entry under 12.
interactions: separate from iron, thyroid medicine, tetracycline and fluoroquinolone antibiotics by 2 hours
medicines.overdose_note: Excessive prolonged use can raise blood calcium (milk-alkali syndrome).
medicines.source: NICE CKS dyspepsia

indications: chesty cough with thick phlegm that is hard to bring up
medicines.adult_dose: 10 mL (200 mg) every 4 hours with plenty of water. Warm fluids and steam help as much as the syrup.
medicines.max_daily_dose: 2400 mg/day (adult).
medicines.paediatric_dose: 6 to 12 years: 5 mL every 4 hours. Not for children under 6.
contraindications: persistent cough lasting more than 3 weeks
cough with breathlessness or chest pain (needs assessment)
interactions: few; avoid combining several cough products
medicines.overdose_note: Large amounts cause vomiting and drowsiness.
medicines.source: NICE CKS cough; WHO Model Formulary

medicines.adult_dose: 2 to 3 drops or 1 to 2 sprays in each nostril as often as needed. Very safe.
medicines.max_daily_dose: No practical limit.
medicines.paediatric_dose: Infants and children: 1 to 2 drops in each nostril before feeds and sleep, then gently clear the nose.
medicines.overdose_note: Not applicable.
medicines.source: NICE CKS common cold; IAP

indications: short-term relief of a badly blocked nose from a cold or sinusitis
medicines.adult_dose: 1 spray or 2 to 3 drops of 0.1% in each nostril up to 3 times a day. Use for no more than 5 to 7 days.
medicines.max_daily_dose: 3 applications per nostril per day.
medicines.paediatric_dose: 6 to 12 years: 0.05% strength, 1 drop per nostril up to 3 times a day, max 5 days. Not for children under 6.
contraindications: use for more than 7 days (causes rebound congestion)
on MAOI antidepressants or within 2 weeks of stopping them
major_side_effects: rise in blood pressure or palpitations
medicines.overdose_note: Swallowed drops, especially by children, can cause dangerous drowsiness, slow heartbeat and low temperature - keep out of reach and seek care if ingested.
medicines.source: NICE CKS common cold; WHO Model Formulary

medicines.adult_dose: 1 lozenge dissolved slowly in the mouth every 2 to 3 hours. Warm salt-water gargles help too.
medicines.max_daily_dose: Usually up to 8 to 12 lozenges/day - follow the pack.
medicines.paediatric_dose: Not for young children (choking risk). 6 years and above only, with supervision.
contraindications: sore throat with high fever, drooling, or difficulty breathing/swallowing (needs urgent assessment)
sore throat lasting more than 1 week
major_side_effects: occasional stomach upset if many are taken
medicines.overdose_note: Eating many at once can cause diarrhoea and stomach ache.
medicines.source: NICE CKS sore throat

indications: cleaning minor cuts, grazes and small wounds
medicines.adult_dose: Rinse the wound with clean water first, then apply to the intact skin around and on the minor wound 1 to 2 times a day. Cover with a clean dressing.
medicines.max_daily_dose: Topical use only; avoid large-area or long-term use.
medicines.paediatric_dose: Same topical use for minor wounds. Avoid on large areas in infants (iodine absorption).
contraindications: thyroid disease (avoid large or repeated use)
deep, dirty, or large wounds, animal or human bites, puncture wounds (need medical care and possibly a tetanus injection)
interactions: do not use together with hydrogen peroxide or silver dressings on the same wound
medicines.overdose_note: Swallowing is harmful - keep away from children.
medicines.source: WHO wound care; NICE CKS lacerations

indications: fungal skin infection with itchy round patches
medicines.adult_dose: Apply a thin layer to the rash and about 2 cm beyond its edge, 2 to 3 times a day. Keep using for 2 weeks AFTER the rash clears (usually 4 weeks total).
medicines.max_daily_dose: Topical; 3 applications/day.
medicines.paediatric_dose: Same topical use for children; supervise application.
contraindications: rash on the scalp or nails (needs oral treatment from a doctor)
widespread rash, or rash not improving after 2 weeks
signs of bacterial infection - spreading redness, pus, fever
medicines.overdose_note: Not applicable for skin use.
medicines.source: NICE CKS fungal skin infection; WHO Model Formulary

medicines.adult_dose: Apply to the itchy area with cotton wool 2 to 4 times a day. Cooling and soothing only.
medicines.max_daily_dose: No fixed limit; topical.
medicines.paediatric_dose: Safe for children topically. Avoid the face and broken skin.
contraindications: rash with fever and feeling very unwell (could be a serious rash)
medicines.overdose_note: Not applicable.
medicines.source: NICE CKS itch; WHO Model Formulary

medicines.adult_dose: Single 400 mg tablet, chewed or with food. For threadworm, repeat once after 2 weeks and treat the whole household.
medicines.max_daily_dose: 400 mg as a single dose for routine deworming.
medicines.paediatric_dose: Over 2 years: single 400 mg dose. 1 to 2 years: 200 mg single dose. Under 1 year: only on a doctor's advice.
interactions: levels raised by cimetidine and some antacids; dexamethasone and praziquantel also raise levels
medicines.overdose_note: Large repeated doses can affect the liver and blood counts.
medicines.source: WHO preventive chemotherapy; National Deworming Day guidelines

medicines.strength: 60 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid (adult)
indications: pregnancy supplementation as advised by an ANM/ASHA
medicines.adult_dose: 1 tablet once daily, ideally on an empty stomach or with vitamin C (lemon water). If it upsets the stomach, take with food.
medicines.max_daily_dose: 1 to 2 tablets/day as advised; do not exceed without medical advice.
medicines.paediatric_dose: Paediatric IFA syrup is dosed by weight - use the government schedule or a doctor's advice, not this entry.
contraindications: known iron overload (haemochromatosis, thalassaemia with iron loading)
interactions: separate from thyroid tablets, tetracycline/fluoroquinolone antibiotics, antacids and calcium by at least 2 hours
medicines.overdose_note: Iron overdose is a leading cause of poisoning deaths in young children - store locked away. A child who swallows adult iron tablets needs emergency care.
medicines.source: Anaemia Mukt Bharat; WHO

indications: supporting recovery with a poor diet
medicines.adult_dose: 1 tablet (500 mg) once daily. It does not cure a cold but is harmless in this dose.
medicines.max_daily_dose: 1000 mg/day from supplements without advice.
medicines.paediatric_dose: Children over 4: 250 mg/day. Younger children get enough from fruit.
contraindications: history of calcium-oxalate kidney stones (high doses)
major_side_effects: stomach upset or loose stools at high doses
medicines.overdose_note: Very high doses cause diarrhoea and may promote kidney stones.
medicines.source: WHO Model Formulary
